defipunkd.value: Control: orange · Ability to exit: tentative orange (3/3 models submitted) · Autonomy: tentative orange · Open Access: green · Verifiability: green
defipunkd.summary: Pendle V2 splits yield-bearing assets into PT/YT via SY wrappers and trades them on a time-decay AMM. The Router V3 and PendleMarketV3 contracts are immutable; SY adapters and several factories are upgradable via a TransparentUpgradeableProxy ProxyAdmin owned by a 3-of-5 Safe with no timelock. Boros is a separate, smaller IRS module on Arbitrum with its own permissioned admin/risk surface.

details.name: Control
details.description: 3-of-5 multisig controls upgrades, no timelock — Assessed by 3 models — Choosing orange because the green steel-man only holds for the immutable parts of the address surface — the upgradable surface (V2 ProxyAdmin reaching SY/factory implementations, MarketFactoryV3.setTreasuryAndFeeReserve at maxReserveFeePercent=100) puts T1 and T2 on the uncontested fast path of a 3-of-5 multisig with zero timelock, which exceeds both the orange-vs-green threshold (T2 reachable with delay <7 days) and the T1-with-Security-Council-7-day path that would otherwise allow green; the multisig is, however, larger than the red 2-of-3 / single-EOA threshold, so red does not fit either.

details.name: Ability to exit
details.description: Exit-like functions and direct access paths are visible, but pause guards, role holders, queue caps, and claim-finalized semantics were not reconstructed. — Exit-like functions and direct access paths are visible, but pause guards, role holders, queue caps, and claim-finalized semantics were not reconstructed.

details.name: Autonomy
details.description: Boros oracle/bot risk; V2 per-market isolated — Assessed by 6 models — Choosing orange because Module V2 holds about $1.602b, approximately 99.3% of Pendle+Boros TVS (grade: orange due per-market external yield-asset dependencies), while Module Boros holds about $10.98m, approximately 0.7% (grade: red/unknown due off-chain oracle and margin/liquidation coupling without verified fallback); weighted overall is orange because the worst dependency is real but currently small relative to total TVS.

details.name: Open Access
details.description: Permissionless contracts, no KYC, multi-path access — Assessed by 3 models — Choosing green because the operative grade inputs are contract admission and independent reachability: official docs/Terms/SDK evidence show direct non-UI access, and no contract-level whitelist/KYC/operator admission gate was found in the representative fetched surfaces; ToS/sanctions restrictions are reported as context.

details.name: Verifiability
details.description: Verified source + multiple top-firm audits — Assessed by 4 models — Choosing green because the conditions for green (verified bytecode on the user-facing core, a public source repo, and ≥1 recognized-firm audit covering currently-deployed contracts) all hold and the orange steel-man reduces to uneven verification across peripheral contracts and a per-component diff that was not run this round — neither downgrades the verifiability posture for the deployed core.

risklayer.summary: Pendle Finance is a yield-trading protocol with roughly $1.15B TVL across 11 chains, tokenizing future yield into Principal Tokens (PT) and Yield Tokens (YT) traded on a custom AMM. It has operated since 2021 with no confirmed direct smart-contract exploit, supported by 15+ audits and $2.5M in active Cantina bug bounties. The main concerns are 45% unverified contracts, a 3-of-5 multisig that can upgrade core logic without timelock, and permissionless market creation that enabled the $27M Penpie ecosystem loss in September 2024. Overall risk is medium-high at 5.7/10.

details.name: Dependency Risk
details.description: Per-asset SY adapters outside core audit scope, LayerZero cross-chain PT bridging with no external oracle fallback, and internal AMM TWAP pricing amplify composability contagion risk.

details.name: Governance Risk
details.description: 3-of-5 Gnosis Safe multisig controls core contracts without upgrade timelock; dual governance architecture and weaker 2-of-4 Optimism threshold create asymmetric cross-chain control.

details.name: Tokenomics Risk
details.description: 64.6M PENDLE still locked in deprecated vePENDLE during sPENDLE migration creates unlock overhang; multisig-controlled gauge emissions and 2% terminal inflation add moderate dilution risk offset by 80% fee buybacks.

details.name: Audit Coverage Risk
details.description: 15+ audits from tier-1 firms with all core H/M findings fixed and $2.5M active Cantina bounties, but derived SY adapters, cross-chain PT infrastructure, and post-2024 upgrades remain partially unaudited.

details.name: Smart Contract Risk
details.description: 45% of discovered contracts are unverified including ProxyAdmin and sPENDLE; Optimism PT OFT Factory is EOA-controlled; core factories use TransparentUpgradeableProxy with no timelock on upgrades.

risklayer.note: Risklayer is in beta and publishes no ordering for its bands, so the figure is shown exactly as reported.

findings.title: 18 Unverified Contracts Across Core Infrastructure
findings.description: 45% of discovered contracts (18/40) have no verified source on their respective block explorers, preventing independent bytecode audit. This includes ProxyAdmin (upgrade authority), sPENDLE (~33M supply), YieldContractFactoryV6 implementation on Ethereum, cross-chain bridge/oracle contracts on Ethereum, and all Pendle deployments on Plasma and HyperEVM.

findings.title: Optimism PT OFT Factory Controlled by EOA
findings.description: The Optimism PT OFT Adapter Factory (0x45Dd4aEcc425b01bf98C567407aB4a4fF3C7d349) owner is 0x1FcCC097db89A86Bfc474A1028F93958295b1Fb7 (Core Deployer), confirmed as an EOA via eth_getCode. This single externally-owned account can reconfigure cross-chain PT bridging on Optimism without multisig protection — a critical single point of failure for spoke-chain PT liquidity.

findings.title: Unverified ProxyAdmin Controls Core Upgradeable Proxies
findings.description: ProxyAdmin (0xA28c08f165116587D4F3E708743B4dEe155c5E64) is unverified but on-chain owns the TransparentUpgradeableProxy admin slots for MarketFactoryV6, SYFactory, PYYtLpOracle, LimitRouter, and YieldContractFactoryV6. ProxyAdmin owner is the 3/5 governance multisig (0x8119EC16...), enabling immediate implementation swaps with no observable timelock delay.

findings.title: sPENDLE Token Bytecode Unverified
findings.description: sPENDLE (0x999999999991E178D52Cd95AFd4b00d066664144) holds ~33.2M tokens in circulation and is owned by the 3/5 governance multisig, but its source is not verified on Etherscan. Mint, burn, and staking mechanics cannot be independently audited despite sPENDLE being the active governance staking token (vePENDLE deprecated).

findings.title: YieldContractFactoryV6 Implementation Unverified on Ethereum
findings.description: YieldContractFactoryV6 proxy (0x3E6EBa46AbC5ab18ED95F6667d8B2fd4020E4637) delegates to implementation 0x21414e68da7658b5b2d9c04b06a1f03055763087 via ProxyAdmin, but neither the factory address nor its implementation is verified on Etherscan. This factory deploys yield contracts (PT/YT) that hold user funds.

findings.title: Cross-Chain Bridge and Oracle Stack Unverified on Ethereum
findings.description: Three Ethereum contracts in the cross-chain PT pipeline are unverified: SenderEndpoint (0x07b1014c...), PT OFT Adapter Factory (0x905aF80C...), and Cross-Chain Exchange Rate Oracle (0xA914c44E...). PT OFT Factory and CrossChainOracle are owned by the 2/5 Dev Multisig; SenderEndpoint by the 3/5 governance multisig. Bridge configuration (setPeer/setOracle equivalents) cannot be audited from source.

findings.title: No Timelock on Proxy Upgrades
findings.description: Core factories, oracles, and routers use OpenZeppelin TransparentUpgradeableProxy pattern with a central ProxyAdmin. On-chain verification shows upgrades can be executed immediately by the 3/5 governance multisig via ProxyAdmin.upgrade() — no timelock contract is interposed between governance and implementation changes.

findings.title: No Timelock on Admin Actions or Upgrades
findings.description: On-chain verification found no TimelockController or delay mechanism on ProxyAdmin, PendleGovernanceProxy (UUPS), or core factory proxies. The 3-of-5 governance multisig can execute upgrades, parameter changes, and batched admin calls via PendleGovernanceProxy.aggregate() immediately. PENDLE token config changes have a 7-day delay, but contract upgrades do not.

findings.title: Cross-Chain Governance Threshold Asymmetry on Optimism
findings.description: Per-chain Gnosis Safe governance proxies use different signer sets and thresholds. Optimism governance Safe (0xa06C863fcf17cA6f24AA81aeA75E23953193fF6A) is 2-of-4, while Ethereum (0x8119…ee1), Arbitrum/Base (0x7877…75Ac), and BSC (0xA066…a9Ec) are 3-of-5 with overlapping signer sets. Optimism is the weakest governance link for chain-specific actions.

findings.title: Per-Asset SY Adapter Contagion
findings.description: Pendle core wraps yield via permissionless Standardized Yield (SY) adapters that call external protocols (Curve, Balancer, Benqi/QiToken, etc.). ChainSecurity and Spearbit audits explicitly exclude derived SY implementations. A compromised or misconfigured SY adapter can poison exchangeRate(), affecting PT/YT pricing, cross-chain oracle feeds, and any integrator relying on Pendle markets.

findings.title: Penpie Third-Party Exploit — Sep 2024 ($27M)
findings.description: On Sep 3, 2024, Penpie (yield optimizer built on Pendle) lost ~$27M via reentrancy in batchHarvestMarketRewards. Attacker created malicious Pendle markets using permissionless market creation with fake SY contracts. Pendle contracts were not exploited; Pendle detected the attack, paused all contracts within ~1 hour, and reportedly prevented ~$70–105M in additional losses across dependent protocol…

findings.title: Cross-Chain Governance Threshold Divergence
findings.description: Governance multisig thresholds differ across chains: Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, and BSC use 3/5, while Optimism uses 2/4. Weaker quorum on Optimism reduces the number of signers required for governance actions on that chain's deployments.
